analysis_packet.certificate: The immutable anchor is an online, standard-library, byte-aware two-segment recency/frequency policy with bounded ghost metadata and an adaptive recent-segment byte target. The terminal call must preserve interface legality, never exceed capacity, return only unique currently cached integer keys, and remain independent of hidden traces, scores, oracle behavior, and external sources. The candidate hypothesis conflicts with the declared Permanent Source-Class Cut: terminal visibility of anchor_policy is not restored, so continuity must be conveyed only through this analysis.
exact_actions: Reconstruct one complete policy from the behavioral witnesses and obligations: bounded byte-aware recent/frequent residency, adaptive recent target, bounded ghost_recent/ghost_frequent metadata, and explicit used-byte accounting.
On each access, normalize key and nonnegative size; distinguish resident hit, recent-ghost hit, frequent-ghost hit, cold miss, and oversized input before choosing admission and eviction behavior.
For resident hits, remove prior accounting, reject an object larger than capacity by returning its removed key, otherwise make room and promote the refreshed object to frequent.

For ghost hits, adjust the recent target using the opposing ghost-byte ratio, remove the ghost record, make room, and admit to frequent; for cold misses, make room and admit to recent unless oversized.
Evict oldest eligible resident entries until the incoming object fits, append each removed key once, and record bounded ghost evidence with its segment classification.
Before returning, ensure resident containers and byte counters are mutually consistent, capacity-safe, and that the returned list contains only integer keys removed during this request.
obligations: Use only standard-library mechanisms and online state from prior accesses; do not inspect or encode evaluator traces, benchmark paths, reference implementations, oracle decisions, or scores.
Implement exactly Policy(capacity_bytes) and access(key, size, now) -> list[int], coercing keys and sizes consistently and treating negative capacity or size as zero.
Keep used bytes equal to resident bytes and enforce used <= max(0, capacity) after every access, including zero-capacity and oversized-object cases.
Return only keys evicted by the current request, each as an integer and at most once; never return a key that is not currently resident before that eviction.
Keep ghost metadata advisory and bounded by both byte and count limits; ghost entries must never count toward resident capacity.
Preserve online phase adaptation through ghost-hit target adjustment while retaining scan resistance via separation of cold recent entries from promoted frequent entries.
The terminal artifact must be one complete policy and must not depend on reacquiring anchor_policy, candidate_hypothesis, loop_structure, or any cut generative source.
witnesses: Anchor maintains resident recent and frequent segments with byte accounting, plus bounded recent/frequent ghost histories.
Resident hits remove the old residency, admit the refreshed object to the frequent segment, and may evict objects until incoming bytes fit.
A ghost hit adapts the recent-segment byte target according to opposing ghost-byte evidence, then admits the object to the frequent segment.
Cold misses enter the recent segment; evictions record key, size, and source segment in bounded ghost metadata.
Objects larger than capacity are not admitted; an oversized resident refresh is removed and returned as the evicted key.
Eviction order is oldest eligible resident entry, preferring recent entries when the recent byte target is exceeded or a recent ghost hit requires it, with fallbacks to the other segment.
